text:
The change logs each forecast request and adds a test for the city in the log. The logged URL also contains the API key: direct execution produced `city=Lyon&key=fake-key-0000`. With INFO logging enabled, real credentials will enter application logs, violating R1.

The new test checks only that the city appears; it passes even when the key leaks. Pytest is unavailable in this environment, so I verified the logging behavior directly.

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "path": "app/weather.py",
      "side": "head",
      "line": 20,
      "end_line": 20,
      "line_text": "        log.info(\"forecast request: %s\", url)",
      "severity": "blocking",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Forecast logging exposes the API key",
      "body": "When INFO logging is enabled, every forecast call writes the API key to application logs because url includes the key query parameter. This violates R1 and exposes credentials to log readers and logging services. The new test checks only city=Lyon and does not assert that the key is absent.",
      "defect_key": "secret_in_logs",
      "suggestion": "        log.info(\"forecast request: %s?%s\", BASE_URL, urlencode({'city': city}))",
      "pre_existing": false,
      "rule": "R1"
    }
  ],
  "empty_reason": null
}
```
